newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA'S TELCOMS MINISTER SEEKS SENTECH TAKEOVER.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA'S TELCOMS MINISTER SEEKS SENTECH TAKEOVER.

text.p: South African Posts and Telecommunications Minister Jay Naidoo asked parliament on Tuesday to transfer control of Sentech (Pty) Ltd from the national broadcaster to the state.

The Sentech Bill tabled by Naidoo proposes that the signal distribution company, until now a wholly-owned subsidiary of the South African Broadcasting Corporation (SABC), be converted into a public company.

The bill makes the state the only member and shareholder, and gives the government power to expropriate Sentech's assets. Sentech, the technical service provider for radio and television, was granted a 15-year licence by the Independent Broadcastng Authority (IBA) in March last year.

Parliament adopted recommendations by the IBA's Triple Inquiry Report on March 28 this year for Sentech to be separated from the SABC and converted into an autonomous public enterprise under the aegis of the telecommunications minister.

The SABC, which is itself state-owned, recently sold off five of its radio stations in a privatisation drive spearheaded by the African National Congress-led government which is trying to restructure state assets and promote fiscal discipline.
